items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I had Joe and Eddie in there... I was responsible for putting them in... we had no problem.

ctx.x: Right, and then I would just leave out a part. They would bring in the singers and they would never call up and say, 'Look, they're going to sing this in such and such a key.' But they would just bring in the singer and I would have the arrangement made and they would say, 'We will cut here, play the verse and before you go into the chorus, Eddie, get us into the key you want and Joe, you and Eddie play the backup, in back of the voices.' You never could tell. We couldn't --unless I could get the part, the rhythm…
So as far as the recording was concerned, I would say that they didn't accomplish what they set out to accomplish.

items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: They also picked out our singers... And then they brought this trio in... but they did bring Joe and Eddie in... Tommy Gott, Arnold Brilhant, Alfie Alphie Evans and Joe and Eddie. He had a real crackerjack band. We used to go over and listen to it.

ctx.x: the band. He didn't want any part of Bix. He didn't want any part of the jazz part of the band. He wanted it to be another Whiteman band, something which he was very successful with. and Eddie King, you know, he and Whiteman and Grofé were like that, all in one, and that was the (sings) which I'm a great favorite of, the oompha at that time, it's kept a good tempo, but that was Grofé's (phonetic) style and it was a style of the Whiteman band.

We had a more, aloofal style, and you couldn't make the one, ours go over into their type of thing, which had been very, very successful. So they come up, they're thinking the tunes can do it. They tried, but they didn't come up with anything. The first tune we got that was like anything like what we could do was "Sunday" and then they brought us a trio. They also picked out our singers, so we had Bix Murray, Frank Bessinger, guys like that although good in their own, they were successful, weren't good with us.…

Now that's more improvising than you can get, but it's a different kind of improvising. Eddie King could probably go along with. It didn't hurt anything. So here we got Eddie right in front of the mike playing his guitar and we got a hell of a fine banjo player down there, Howdy Quicksell and
